# Preserve a supported rule when documenting scoped exceptions

A scoped exception limits where a rule applies. Keep the supported rule and record the exception with its condition, component, behavior and source. Do not reverse a general preference because one local example uses another form.

Changing a learned preference needs evidence that accepted practice changed or that the supposed earlier preference was never supported. Keep the reason and contrary evidence. Reviewer uncertainty, an isolated counterexample, or a historical exception alone does not establish such a change.

User-directed rules remain in force until the user deliberately changes them. Automatic study must not edit them. For example, the sparse row-cache reason for Array.prototype.forEach is a scoped exception; it does not remove the current for...of preference for ordinary iteration with actions.

This is a direct user clarification during the history study. It is not a new convention inferred from commit counts or an old review. It applies to knowledge capture, code writing, verification and review.
title: Preserve a supported rule when documenting scoped exceptions
